passage: In 2018, marine engineer Dionte Harmon and his team at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution set out to build an underwater vehicle capable of operating in the deepest ocean trenches. Because the water pressure at extreme depths is over 1,000 times greater than at sea level, standard underwater vehicles would be crushed by the immense pressure before reaching the ocean floor. For four years, Harmon's team tested designs in a pressure chamber that simulated deep-sea conditions. The vehicle the team ultimately designed can withstand the crushing depths because its hull is thicker and uses stronger materials than those of a submersible of the same size built for shallow water operations.
prompt: According to the text, why would an underwater vehicle built for shallow water be unable to operate in the deepest ocean trenches?

choices.A: Because the hulls of vehicles built for shallow water are too thick to work in deep ocean trenches
choices.B: Because the deepest ocean trenches and shallow water have different pressure conditions
choices.C: Because the temperature of deep ocean trenches is much colder than the temperature of shallow water
choices.D: Because vehicles built for shallow water are too small to handle the conditions in deep ocean trenches

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents an explanation about an underwater vehicle that is directly supported by the text. The text states that water pressure at extreme depths is over 1,000 times greater than at sea level, and as a result, standard underwater vehicles would be crushed by the immense pressure before reaching the ocean floor. In other words, a vehicle built for shallow water can't operate in deep trenches because of the differences in the two environments' pressure conditions.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because the text doesn't indicate that vehicles built for shallow water are too small to operate in the conditions of deep ocean trenches. In fact, the text states that the size of the vehicle built to operate in deep trenches is the same size as a vehicle built for shallow water, even though it has a thicker hull that uses stronger materials.
